result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.count_strongly_connected_components()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Count strongly connected components. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L21606-L21671){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.count_strongly_connected_components() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![SCC vs. WCC](/assets/graphs/algo-scc-vs-wcc.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The same directed graph shown twice. On the left, the strongly connected components: A, B, and C form a directed cycle and share one accent tint, while D and E are each their own singleton component, shown in a lighter accent tint. On the right, ignoring edge directions collapses everything into a single weakly connected component, and all five nodes share the same accent color." width="100%"} For directed graphs, a strongly connected component is a maximal set of nodes where every node is reachable from every other node following directed edges. Uses Kosaraju's algorithm for efficient computation. For undirected graphs, returns the same result as `count_weakly_connected_components()` since strong connectivity equals regular connectivity when edges are bidirectional. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of strongly connected components. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} A directed cycle keeps all its nodes mutually reachable, forming one strongly connected component, while a separate pair connected by a single one-way edge can't reach back and so forms its own component: ::: {#31eb6ced .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_node(label="X") .add_node(label="Y") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("B", "C") .add_edge("C", "A") # Cycle: all in same component .add_edge("X", "Y") # Separate component ) # Returns 2 graph.count_strongly_connected_components() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 3 ``` ::: ::: For undirected graphs, every edge is bidirectional, so strong and weak connectivity give the same answer: ::: {#8814c2ca .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=False) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="X") .add_edge("A", "B") ) # Returns 2 graph.count_strongly_connected_components() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 2 ``` ::: ::: ::: {#e261331b .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Returns 2 (same result as strongly connected, since edges are bidirectional) graph.count_weakly_connected_components() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` 2 ``` ::: :::
